independent.summary: Treating `session-ended` as a permanent stop breaks "Sign out everywhere else": `POST /auth/revoke-other-sessions` calls `closeStreamsForUser(userId)`, which closes the caller's OWN stream with `{ error: 'session-ended' }` (server/src/routes/auth.js:1216, whose comment explicitly relies on "the caller's client reconnects within seconds and is accepted, because its session was re-stamped above"). The still-signed-in tab now sets `stopped = true`, never reconnects, and toasts "you were signed out in another window" — live sync is dead for the rest of that tab's life and the message is false.

The two bulk handlers only call `loadEntities`, which rebuilds the sidebar list but never touches `selectedEntity` or the open panels (unlike `onEntityUpdated`, which replaces `selectedEntity`), so an entity a user has open that another client's draft apply edited keeps showing pre-apply content indefinitely.

`STOP_REASONS[reason]` is an unguarded property lookup on a server-supplied string, so inherited keys are truthy: a frame carrying `{ error: 'toString' }` (or `constructor`, `valueOf`) is treated as a permanent stop and reported with a garbage message, instead of taking the deliberate "unknown code is retried" path — `Object.hasOwn` / a `Map` is what the stated rule needs.

grades.reason: The message is built by `STOP_REASONS['too-many-streams']` and names the limit (`useEvents.js:97`), and the layout toasts that `message` verbatim; the composable's test asserts the limit appears.
`onFrame` wraps `JSON.parse` in try/catch, logs at the light tier and returns without calling the handler — an unparseable frame is handled, and no handler sees a missing payload.

`onStreamEnded?.()` is the final statement of the error path, nothing follows it, and the only registered handler is an `addToast` call — the described failure has no consequence in this code (and the finding contradicts itself about whether it is caught).
`log('verbose'/'normal')` is gated by `LEVELS`, so at the default `light` tier no payload is printed; the test asserting exactly this passes (I ran the suite).

`WikiLayout.test.js` ('WikiLayout live sync') asserts `loadEntities` is called once with a reason matching /draft/i and /import/i for both frames; the composable suite correctly asserts only handler invocation.
The same WikiLayout group asserts `addToast` was called once per frame, with the actor label and the counts in the message.
`docs/api.md` adds a "The frames" table whose rows include `workspace:imported` (sent by `POST /import`, carrying `{ version, imported, actor }`).

The actor label comes from the DB via `requireActor` (the member's own email), is broadcast only to streams already scoped to that workspace, and is identical to what every existing `entity:*` frame carries — no untrusted input and no new disclosure.

triageGrades.reason: The change adds `requireActor` to `POST /import` (a new 401 path) and rewrites how the client reacts to `session-ended`/revocation frames, so auth is touched.
No credential, token, key or secret is read, stored or logged anywhere in the diff; the tiered logging concerns entity content, not secrets.
Nothing in the diff touches the AI allowance, billing or cost accounting.
The diff adds a broadcast and client listeners; no delete, overwrite or data-removing path is introduced (the test helper that empties a workspace is pre-existing).
Only the app's own `/events` and `/import` endpoints are involved — no third-party service call.
No version bump, deploy config or new required environment variable; the new client tier is a `localStorage` key.

summary: All eight local findings are false positives — several assert the absence of things the diff plainly contains (the docs table row, the `loadEntities`/`addToast` assertions, the limit-naming message) — and the review missed the one real regression, that the new permanent-stop handling of `session-ended` kills live sync in the tab that uses "Sign out everywhere else".
